max_tire.note: The Portal Hub sweet spot. 265/75R16 is about stock height; 285/75R16 fits but rubs at full lock, and owners call 33s the practical maximum before the right front rubs.

max_tire.size: 235/85R16–255/85R16 on 16 x 6.5 Ford Transit steel wheels
max_tire.note: Tubeless with safety beads. Owners estimate the offset puts the tire about 15 mm further out than the stock rim, and Fat Fabrications' disc-brake kits use these wheels.

timeline.change: Steyr-Daimler-Puch starts developing a bigger brother to the Haflinger
Series production of the 710 (4x4) and 712 (6x6) begins; 167 built that year
Yugoslavia begins buying what becomes 3,975 Pinzgauers across 4x4 and 6x6 variants
Owners report SDP added insulation to the intake runners during 1973 production, reducing hot-restart vapor lock
Peak year for the first generation: 2,430 built
The 712 6x6 outsells the 710 for the first time (580 vs 312), and keeps doing so through 1985
Some 712s, mostly ambulances, get a 2.7-liter air-cooled four
Last 710s (90) and 712s (326) built; the first six Turbo D 716/718s appear

identify.intro: The 710/712 barely changed in 15 years, so identification comes down to wheels, body code, engine and which army a truck served with. Don't confuse a petrol truck with a later Turbo D.

items.head: 710 vs 712
items.body: Count the axles. The 710 is the 4x4 on a 2,200 mm wheelbase with rear coil springs. The 712 is the 6x6, with a leaf-sprung rear bogie on a 2,000 + 980 mm wheelbase.

items.head: Body codes
items.body: M is the soft top with rear bench seats, K the hardtop station wagon, T the flatbed and AMB the ambulance (AMB-Y, or AMB-S with an air-portable shelter). On the 712 there are also W (workshop), DK (crew cab), FW (fire truck) and FLA.

items.head: Petrol 710/712 vs Turbo D 716/718
items.body: The 710/712 has the air-cooled 2.5-liter petrol four, a five-speed manual, drum brakes and narrower tires. The 716/718 (from 1985) has a water-cooled VW turbodiesel six, disc brakes, a slightly wider track, bigger tires and an optional automatic.

items.head: Swiss vs Austrian trucks
items.body: Swiss trucks have a single amber bulb for turn and brake plus a red tail lamp. Austrian trucks have amber turn signals with separate red brake and tail lamps. Swiss 710K radio command trucks (Funkkommandowagen) have their own wiring.

items.head: Engine
items.body: Check the engine plate and bore. The standard engine is 2,499 cc (92 x 94 mm). Late 712s, mostly ambulances, can have the 2.7-liter air-cooled four.

capability.note: Off-road: 1,500 kg (3,307 lb) for the 710, 1,800 kg (3,968 lb) for the 712
Factory figures; owners quoted by OffGrid report 15–16 mpg

values.intro: Prices are steady and still affordable for something this capable. Condition, rust and how sorted the truck is matter far more than year, a 712 6x6 adds a few thousand dollars, and celebrity provenance can double the price.
values.note: Based on 16 Bring a Trailer sales of 710s and 712s from 2023 to October 2026 ($9,500–$32,500; most 710s $10,500–$18,000, 712s $9,500–$24,250). No-sale high bids ran $9,300–$19,500. A 2019 Portal Hub estimate put 710Ms at $5k–18k, and Swiss Army Vehicles was asking $24,900 for a 1974 712M in October 2026.

paragraphs: Steyr never sold the 710/712 new in the US, so every American truck is a used import, almost always ex-military. Most are ex-Swiss Army, with some ex-Austrian. Every 710 and 712 is now more than 40 years old, comfortably past the 25-year line that lets an older vehicle into the US without meeting federal safety standards. OffGrid noted in 2017 that early Pinzgauers are old enough to be exempt from many US import equipment requirements.

The model-specific question is paperwork. Ask for the import entry, any Swiss or Austrian registration or army documents, and a US title in the seller's name. The ex-Lutz 710M that sold on BaT in 2026 came with a Swiss registration document and a clean Texas title. Established dealers such as Swiss Army Vehicles in Arkansas have sold ex-military trucks for more than 20 years. Rules for registering former military vehicles vary by state, so check with your DMV before you buy.
